“I was in the refinery’s central control room during Hurricane Delta when a call came in over the radio from the Sheriff’s Department. They called us at the refinery to ask if anyone there could help rescue a woman and her two dogs trapped in a flooded car on Old Spanish Trail not far from the refinery. The Sheriff’s Department and Westlake Fire Department couldn’t reach the individual and they asked us for help.” ~Sean Smith, Operations Manager, Phillips 66 Lake Charles Refinery

“Without hesitation, the three of us jumped into the refinery’s high-clearance fire truck and drove to the scene. Driving at night with high winds and severe flooding, there were several road hazards. We even had to swerve to avoid a trampoline that was in the middle of the road. We quickly spotted the car that was submerged in about four feet of water.” ~Chris Dailey, Safety and Emergency Response Team Lead, Phillips 66 Lake Charles Refinery

“We were able to pull the woman and her two dogs from the car, and then transport her to the local Westlake Fire Station. Even though the Fire Station was less than two miles from the refinery, our trip there was anything but easy, we had to maneuver through 45-mph winds and downed power lines. Ironically, on the way back to the Fire Station, the dogs were calm - albeit wetter than normal.” ~Zach Evans, HSE Specialist, Phillips 66 Lake Charles Refinery

Sean, Chris, and Zach's stories are  part of our "Humans of the Industry" series.

text:
It was 10 years ago that Hilcorp made its entry into Alaska and what an impact it’s made. Hilcorp is now the largest field operator in the state, based on operated oil and gas volume. It operates more than 1,700 producing wells, with gross production of about 345,000 barrels of oil/day and 150 million cubic feet of gas/day.

“We’re here to grow for decades to come,” Jill Fisk, Hilcorp Alaska senior asset team leader for Prudhoe Bay west, told the Resource Development Council’s annual conference.

At Prudhoe Bay, Hilcorp has halted the massive field’s 4%/year production decline without any major projects or drilling any new wells. It has experienced world-class results from Milne Point’s viscous oil in Schrader Bluff and is taking its polymer flooding technology to Prudhoe Bay.

“Alaska has clearly been a big win for Hilcorp, but we also believe our success in Alaska is a big win for Alaska and the people that live here,” Fisk said. You can watch Fisk’s entire presentation here. https://vimeo.com/647472375.
